admissibility_topology_transition.description: Formal scaffold for topological transitions of admissibility regions under process dynamics.
core_principles: Admissibility manifolds are dynamic and deform under parameter shifts (epsilon, residue, orientation).
Transitions occur when the connectedness, boundary count, or genus of an admissibility region changes.
Collapse or bifurcation events indicate structural instability or process state transitions.

transition_classes.name: boundary_deformation
transition_classes.description: Continuous shifting of the admissibility boundary without topological change.

transition_classes.name: boundary_split
transition_classes.description: A single connected admissibility region splits into disjoint components.
transition_classes.geometry: Increase in the count of connected components.

transition_classes.name: boundary_merge
transition_classes.description: Disjoint admissibility regions merge into a single connected basin.
transition_classes.geometry: Decrease in the count of connected components.

transition_classes.name: admissibility_basin_collapse
transition_classes.description: Complete erasure of an admissible region; process termination or singularity hit.
transition_classes.geometry: Measure of the admissibility set goes to zero.

transition_classes.name: epsilon_null_bifurcation
transition_classes.description: Splitting or merging of continuation branches exactly at the epsilon-null singularity.
transition_classes.geometry: Bifurcation of the manifold at a singular point.
